alice: Quick follow-up from the RFC: after enabling lazy hydration we see 99.9th token latency spikes on cold shards. Baseline p99 ~180ms, now jumps to ~2.4s on first hit.

ben: Can you paste the query pattern or a snippet of the trace? Is the spike happening during disk read or the kV cache sync?

alice: Trace attached inline — looks like long stall on `read_shard_chunk()` followed by a synchronous GPU memcpy. Example stack: `hotstart.coordinator -> loader.hot_fill -> read_shard_chunk -> mmap_read -> gpu_upload_sync`.

carol: That matches what I saw in dev canaries. Lazy hydration reduces steady-state memory pressure but introduces serialized blocking on the first request for a shard. Evictions + lazy on rare shards -> repeated cold spikes.

dave: Could be two separate problems: (1) blocking GPU upload path, (2) no backoff/queueing when multiple in-flight requests touch same missing shard. We should avoid thundering herd into `gpu_upload_sync`.

alice: Agreed. I prototyped a hybrid 'on-demand but async' path: kick off async prefetch + return a soft-accept token to requestor; first token waits for a small fence (50ms) then falls back to synchronous if not ready. Early numbers reduce tail by ~40% on our synthetic workload but increases memory churn slightly.

ben: Interesting. Do you have the microbenchmark? What happens with concurrent requests (N>8) for same shard?

alice: Microbench: `wrk -c 64 -t 8` hitting a model with 12 shards. When N_concurrent hits same shard=16, previous lazy -> 5x p99 spike; hybrid async -> 1.8x p99 with most requests served from async completion.

carol: Sounds promising. We should also add request coalescing per-shard: one active upload, others wait on a future instead of each starting uploads. That will limit IO and GPU transfer duplication.

dave: +1 for coalescing. Also we need metrics: `first_request_latency_by_shard`, `concurrent_hydration_attempts`, `hydration_queue_latency`. Without those we can't tune the fence wait.

warmup-bot: AUTO: canary created — hybrid-hydration-10pct (traffic=10%). Logs forwarding to #eng-ml-canaries.

ben: Two safety tradeoffs: (A) hybrid increases mem footprint temporarily because async prefetch may bring in shards that are rarely used, (B) coalescing + async requires robust cancellation when eviction kicks in mid-upload. We need a lease model: hydration holds a short-lived lease that prevents eviction until upload finishes or cancels.

carol: For lease semantics: make them lightweight (epoch id + expiry). If eviction sees an active lease, it can either extend lease or queue the eviction until lease expiry. Eviction should not block critical SLOs though.

alice: Implementation note: use per-shard atomic state machine: {MISSING, PENDING(async_id), READY, EVICTING}. PENDING carries a list of waiters (futures). On cancel/evict we notify waiters with a specific error so callers can fallback to alternative shards/models.

dave: Error handling needs to surface a sentinel so higher-level routing can fallback to smaller model variant or a cached prefix. Suggested error: `HydrationCancelledByEviction`.

ben: Ops question: do we want warmup-bot to proactively prefetch popular shards (prediction-based) into dedicated pools to keep predictable latency? That's the older warmup idea but more aggressive.

carol: Prediction-based warmup helps for steady-state hot keys but costs memory. Maybe combine with usage heatmap + TTL: prefetch if a shard crosses threshold X hits/min for Y minutes.

alice: Action items: 1) Ben -> add metrics (`first_request_latency_by_shard`, `concurrent_hydration_attempts`, `hydration_queue_latency`) by end of week. 2) Carol -> design lease + state machine sketch and failure semantics. 3) Dave -> prototype coalescing guard and async upload path; instrument mem delta. 4) Alice -> run hybrid-hydration canary results after 24h and post numbers.

ben: I'll start a PR for metrics and add a dashboard panel for quick triage.

carol: I'll draft a brief RFC addendum about lease timeout heuristics and eviction policy interactions.

alice: Thanks — let's sync in the 1pm eng-ml meeting if we have preliminary numbers. :thumbsup:

warmup-bot: NOTE: canary hybrid-hydration-10pct created at 1750004328, status: running. Logs -> s3://redwood-canaries/hybrid-hydration/1750004328

dave: One more: include a debug flag to force synchronous hydration per-request for deterministic tests (`X-Hydration: sync`). Helps reproduce.

alice: Good call. I'll add that to the canary endpoint.

ben: Cool. If hybrid + coalescing looks stable we should fold into default lazy strategy but gate behind tenant opts and a global mem budget knob.

carol: Agreed. End-to-end tests next.
